summary: This lecture reaches the day the Prophet Muhammad SAW was born. The ustaz recalls the marriage of Abdullah and Aminah bint Wahb, the slave girl Ummu Aiman, Abdullah's journey to Sham and his death in Yathrib while Aminah was pregnant. The Prophet SAW was born on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant, welcomed by Ummu Aiman, and Abdul Muttalib named him Muhammad. He was nursed by his mother, by Thuwaibah and then by Halimah of Banu Sa'd, who in the end took him in, and her home and animals were filled with blessing. The lecture ends with the two angels who opened his chest when he was a little over three years old.
keyPoints: Abdullah married Aminah bint Wahb and gave her a slave girl named Barakah, later known as Ummu Aiman.
Abdullah died in Yathrib on the way back from Sham, when the Prophet SAW was about two months in the womb.
The Prophet SAW was born on a Monday, in Rabi' al-Awwal, in the Year of the Elephant, and Ummu Aiman welcomed him.
Abdul Muttalib named him Muhammad, meaning the praised one, so that he would be praised on earth and in the heavens.
Halimah of Banu Sa'd took him as her foster child, and her provision and animals grew full of blessing.
At a little over three years old, two angels opened his chest and washed his heart with zamzam water.

chapters.title: Opening and a recap of the last lecture
chapters.summary: The lecture moves on to the day the Prophet SAW was born, after recalling Abraha's attack and the story of Abdullah who was nearly sacrificed.

chapters.title: Abdullah marries Aminah, and the slave girl Ummu Aiman
chapters.summary: Abdullah married Aminah bint Wahb and bought a young slave girl named Barakah, later known as Ummu Aiman.

chapters.title: Abdullah leaves for Sham and Aminah has a dream
chapters.summary: A week after the wedding Abdullah went trading to Sham. Aminah became pregnant and dreamed that a light came out of her womb as far as Syria.

chapters.title: Abdullah dies in Yathrib
chapters.summary: Abdullah fell ill with a high fever in Yathrib, stayed with his grandmother's family, and died. Aminah was very sad and Ummu Aiman stayed by her.

chapters.title: The awaited orphan
chapters.summary: The ustaz explains what an orphan is, and that the baby in the womb was then only two months along.

chapters.title: The birth of the Prophet SAW
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW was born at full term and welcomed by Ummu Aiman, with a light that lit the house as far as Sham.

chapters.title: The day, month and date of his birth
chapters.summary: He was born on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal. The exact date is unknown because people then did not register births.

chapters.title: Thuwaibah and Abu Lahab
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab's slave Thuwaibah brought news of the birth, and Abu Lahab freed her out of joy.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib names him Muhammad
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib took the baby to the Kaaba, prayed, and named him Muhammad so that he would be praised on earth and in the heavens.

chapters.title: Nursed by Aminah and Thuwaibah, and the hadith on Ibrahim's prayer
chapters.summary: He was nursed by his mother and by Thuwaibah and circumcised on the seventh day, and the ustaz cites the hadith about Ibrahim's prayer.

chapters.title: Halimah and the custom of wet nurses
chapters.summary: Halimah of Banu Sa'd, hit by drought, came to Mecca looking for a baby to nurse. Babies were sent to the countryside for clean air and pure Arabic.

chapters.title: Halimah's journey to Mecca
chapters.summary: Halimah arrived last on a weak donkey, and every baby that had a father had already been taken.

chapters.title: Halimah takes baby Muhammad
chapters.summary: Halimah decided to take the orphan baby, and her milk became plentiful and her camel and donkey strong.

chapters.title: Blessing in the village of Banu Sa'd
chapters.summary: Halimah's garden and goats flourished while other villages stayed in drought. The Prophet SAW had a foster sister, Shaimah, and stayed for over four years.

chapters.title: His chest is opened
chapters.summary: While playing, an angel opened his chest, washed his heart with zamzam water and removed a black part. The story continues in the next lecture.

lessons.title: Caring for orphans
lessons.body: An orphan is a child who has lost his father and can easily feel alone, so orphans need to be looked after.

lessons.title: Loyal help for the family
lessons.body: Ummu Aiman looked after Aminah's household and stayed with her through her grief.

lessons.title: Having someone to share your feelings with
lessons.body: Aminah poured out her sadness to Ummu Aiman, which shows how important it is to have someone beside you in loss.

lessons.title: What matters is the year and the day of his birth
lessons.body: The exact date of the Prophet's birth is unknown, but the Year of the Elephant, a Monday and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal are known with certainty.

lessons.title: Fasting on Mondays
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW fasted on Mondays because he was born on that day.

lessons.title: Giving a good name
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib named his grandson Muhammad so that he would be praised on earth and in the heavens.

lessons.title: A clean environment helps raise a child
lessons.body: Babies were sent to the countryside for clean air and water, and the Arabic there was pure, so the Prophet's Arabic was excellent.

lessons.title: Taking in the one nobody wanted brings provision
lessons.body: Halimah took the orphan everyone had left behind, and her husband Al-Harith said perhaps Allah would grant them provision.

lessons.title: Allah plans in the best way
lessons.body: Halimah's garden and animals flourished while others suffered drought, because Allah had planned provision for whoever took baby Muhammad.

lessons.title: The Prophet's heart was purified
lessons.body: The angel washed the Prophet's heart with zamzam water, removed a black part and put it back.

dalil.context: The ustaz cites this hadith to show the Prophet SAW was born on a Monday and that fasting on Mondays is a way of celebrating it. He does not name a narrator or source.
dalil.translation: Asked why he fasted on Mondays, the Prophet SAW replied that he was born on that day.

dalil.context: The ustaz quotes this hadith to explain the names Muhammad and Ahmad and where he was nursed. The full text is shown here.
dalil.translation: The companions said to him: "Tell us about yourself." He said: "Yes. I am the supplication of my father Ibrahim and the glad tidings brought by Isa, peace be upon them both. My mother saw, when she was carrying me, that a light came out of her that lit up the palaces of Sham. I was nursed among the Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr. While I was with the lambs, two men in white came to me with a golden basin full of snow. They laid me down, split open my belly, took out my heart and split it, took a black clot out of it and threw it away. Then they washed my heart and my belly with that snow and put them back as they were. One said to his companion: 'Weigh him against ten of his community.' They weighed me against ten and I outweighed them. Then: 'Weigh him against a hundred of his community.' I outweighed them. Then: 'Weigh him against a thousand of his community.' I outweighed them. Then he said: 'Leave him. If you weighed him against his whole community, he would outweigh them.'"
